stories.title: Armenian law on EU membership was public initiative, no need for referendum — PM
stories.summary: BISHKEK, September 1. The Armenian law on accession to the European Union was initiated by the people, so its passing precludes the need for a referendum, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek. "To be honest, the passage of the law already signaled that the idea of a referendum was dropped, because if parliament had not passed this law back then - I would like to remind you that this law was initiated by civil society, which means that they collected signatures from Armenian citizens, as the constitution allows, and submitted this bill to parliament. If parliament had not passed this law, the initiators could have collected 250,000 signatures more, and if parliament had rejected it again, we would have had to hold a referendum in Armenia. In other words, by passing this law, we effectively abandoned the idea of a referendum," Pashinyan explained. Earlier during the meeting, Putin called on Pashinyan to let his country's people vote on accession to the European Union and close the topic. "People must always have a choice," Putin stressed. "Well, then, make it, and we'll put this issue to rest That's all. The simplest thing to do is to ask the people, ‘What do you want?’ And that's it.".

stories.title: 'We'll find way to save Jodrell Bank,' Burnham says
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has vowed to save the UK's largest telescope at the Jodrell Bank Observatory. The Lovell telescope, which has stood in Cheshire since 1957, is the world's third-largest steerable radio telescope. But in July this year, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) said the site would not be prioritised for further funding after its current agreement ended in March 2028. Burnham said: "Every one of my generation went on a school trip to Jodrell Bank, and there is no way that we can see its demise, and it won't happen under my government." UKRI said its decision for the site was "the result of a comprehensive, evidence-based prioritisation process". The Prime Minister spoke of his determination to save the site after being asked a question about its future in the House of Commons. Congleton MP Sarah Russell, whose constituency includes the Jodrell Bank site, said it "is facing a significant problem in the medium term because of funding cuts". She called on Burnham and No 10 North to work alongside her and Macclesfield MP Tim Roca to address the issue. Burnham said: "I know there are changes that have been made in relation to research funding, but Jodrell Bank is a heritage asset for the country, as well as a research asset." He said he would set up the meeting she requested, adding: "There must be a way to save Jodrell Bank, and I give a commitment today, at this despatch box, we will find it." The Jodrell Bank site was first established in 1945 and pioneered radio astronomy and the study of galaxies beyond our own. The site has also been immortalised in popular science fiction productions from the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy to Doctor.

stories.title: US strikes Jiroft airport in southern Iran — TV
stories.summary: TEHRAN, September 1. The United States has struck the civilian airport in the city of Jiroft in Iran’s southern Kerman province, the Iranian state television reported. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) said earlier that se series of strikes had been delivered on targets in Iran. According to Press TV, several blasts rocked Iran’s southern coast, including the island of Qeshm and a number of coastal cities.
